title: Chapter XXXIV

teacherSummary.text: Darcy unexpectedly proposes, insulting her family and confessing he loves her against his will. I read “had you behaved in a more gentleman-like manner” slowly and put it in my own words: Elizabeth tells Darcy his proposal only spared her the guilt she might have felt in refusing him, had he behaved in a more gentleman-like manner. Why does Elizabeth's rejection wound Darcy so deeply? My answer: Elizabeth's rejection wounds Darcy so deeply because she says he behaved in an ungentlemanlike manner, attacking his pride in his own conduct; the insult forces Darcy to examine his manners.
